object.name: evi.overdrive.env~
object.digest: Anti-aliased passive tanh-like input/output saturation with optional envelope follower
object.description: A memoryless nonlinear approximation with antiderivative and oversampled processing. Can handle high gain input and remains well anti-aliased. An optional envelope follower allows for dynamic saturation.
object.discussion: For more information about evieve Overdrive processors and other saturation types see the 'evieve overdrive' tab of the helpfile. For more envelope following based saturation see <o>evi.valve~</o>.

inlets.description: Apply gain to engage nonlinearity, applied post envelope detection and pre saturator.

outlets.digest: Buzzy-tanh(x) Out - anti-aliased for your audio not for Maths

outlets.description: If the @follow attribute is on, this outlet will output the automatic gain envelope used on the input to the saturation stage.

attributes.name: aa
attributes.description: The 'aa' ('Anti-Aliasing) method used. 0=Adaa1, 1=Adaa1 2x oversampled, 2=Adaa1 4x oversampled, 3=Adaa2 (default), 4=Adaa2 2x oversampled, 5=Adaa2 4x oversampled. 0..5 does not necessarily mean increasing in quality, it really depends on your audio input material. Experimentation is encouraged.

attributes.name: follow
attributes.description: Engage an envelope follower on the input which dynamically controls gain into the saturation stage.

attributes.name: hfcompensate
attributes.description: The object provides a high frequency compensation 'decorelation' filter on its output for restoring the reduced high frequency response that can occur with this type of anti-aliasing, especially when utilising the oversampling options (as opposed to just using pure 'adaa'). Experiment with turning this on to improve high frequencies (default on).
